name: Dolby Laboratories, Inc.
one_line_reason: The market stopped paying a growth premium for a mature royalty stream tied to flat TV, phone and PC shipments; at a 4.3% owner-cash yield with flat FY27 guidance it is fairly priced, not cheap.
evidence: FY26 (ended 2026-09-25) revenue rose 5% to $1.42B and GAAP EPS 3% to $2.70, but FY27 guidance calls for revenue 'roughly flat at approximately $1.42B' and GAAP EPS $2.67-2.82 (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-17). Licensing is 93% of revenue and 78% of it comes from TVs/set-top boxes (34%), phones (21%), consumer electronics (11%) and PCs (11%), all unit-driven and mature (10-K filed 2026-11-17); the 10-K also flags AI-driven memory shortages raising costs for the devices Dolby is paid on. Ten-year revenue CAGR is 3.3% and five-year EPS CAGR is -1.9%, while stock pay runs $130M a year (9% of revenue). New CEO Marc Whitten joined August 2026.
key_numbers: P/E 20.6 vs 27.0 10y median; EV/EBIT 15.6 vs 23.1; FCF yield 6.8%, FCF-SBC yield 4.3%; rev CAGR 10y 3.3%; EPS CAGR 5y -1.9%; FY27 rev guide flat; net cash $0.58B; short interest 13.6%

name: Graco Inc.
one_line_reason: Two years of soft US housing and construction volumes plus margin dilution from a loss-making acquisition stalled earnings, and a Q3 2026 miss with a light Q4 guide knocked the stock ~15% in a day; the franchise itself is intact.
evidence: Q3 2026 sales rose 8% to $586M (4 points organic, 4 acquired) but gross margin fell about 3 points on higher product costs, lower-margin acquired operations and mix; Valco Melton (adhesives, Industrial segment) added $12M sales and a $5M operating loss (10-Q filed 2026-10-21). Year-to-date volume and price was 0% in the Americas and -3% in EMEA, and the three-year revenue CAGR is 1.4% with net income stuck at $0.46-0.52B since 2022. On 2026-11-10 the company signed a $600M accelerated buyback (about 5% of market cap), funded partly with revolver debt (8-K filed 2026-11-10).
key_numbers: P/E 22.0 vs 28.1 10y median; P/FCF 18.0 vs 27.8; FCF-SBC yield 5.3%; OM 27.9% (10y med 26.6%); ROIC 20.9% vs 30% 5y avg; rev CAGR 3y 1.4%; -23.6% from 3y high

name: Logitech International S.A.
one_line_reason: A one-off chip-supplier fire hits the holiday quarter, but the stock already trades at its own ten-year multiple for a peripherals maker growing low single digits, so there is no discount to find.
evidence: Q2 FY27 (quarter to 2026-09-30) sales rose 3% to $1.22B with GAAP gross margin up 150bp to 44.9% and $406M returned to shareholders (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-10-27). The Q3 FY27 guide is sales of $1.36-1.43B, -5% to 0% in constant currency, including a $70-80M hit because a semiconductor supplier's plant closed after an incident at the end of June 2026; management expects it 'largely resolved by Q4'. Revenue is still below the FY2021 pandemic peak ($5.48B vs $4.84B latest FY), five-year revenue CAGR is -1.6% and five-year EPS CAGR -2.7%.
key_numbers: P/E 20.1 vs 19.2 10y median; EV/EBIT 16.7 vs 18.0; FCF-SBC yield 6.0%; net cash $1.41B; shares -13.7% in 5y; rev CAGR 5y -1.6%; -18.9% from 3y high

name: Gartner, Inc.
one_line_reason: Existing clients are spending less on Gartner's research seats every year (wallet retention fell from 102-108% in 2023 to 98-99% in 2026) just as AI tools offer a cheap substitute for analyst advice, so a former 12%-growth subscription is now a 2.5%-growth one.
evidence: Q3 2026 revenue fell 1.3% to $1.505B and contract value grew only 2.5% FX-neutral to $5.3B (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-03). GTS wallet retention was 98% at 2026-09-30 versus 102% at 2023-09-30, and GBS wallet retention fell to 99% from 102% a year earlier and 108% in 2023 (10-Q filed 2026-11-03; 10-Q filed 2024-11-05); new clients, not existing ones, drove the growth. The stock fell about 31% in one day after Q4 2025, when wallet retention first dropped below 100% and US federal cuts hit; management is offsetting with $1.7B of buybacks in four quarters, partly debt-funded (net debt $1.35B).
key_numbers: P/E 15.5 vs 42.3 10y median; P/FCF 8.7 vs 24.8; FCF-SBC yield 10.1%; CV growth +2.5% (was double-digit); GTS wallet retention 98% (102% in 2023); -67.6% from 3y high; short interest 14.1%

name: Fidelity National Information Services, Inc.
one_line_reason: Two 2026 guidance cuts (bank conversion delays plus a security and implementation spending bump that runs through 2027), a departing CFO and $20.8B of debt from the January 2026 Issuer Solutions deal turned a low-growth bank processor into a levered equity the market priced at under 5x adjusted earnings.
evidence: Q3 2026 pro forma revenue grew 3.7% (recurring +2.5%) and free cash flow rose 8% to $862M, but full-year pro forma growth was cut to 3.1-3.6% from 4.5-5% and adjusted EPS growth to 1.2-2.4% ($5.82-5.89); buybacks are paused until gross leverage reaches about 2.8x and debt stood at $20.8B on 2026-09-30 (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-04). The $13.5B Issuer Solutions purchase from Global Payments closed 2026-01-09 (10-Q filed 2026-11-04); an earlier cut on 2026-08-04 hit Capital Markets, and the stock fell roughly 20% on 2026-11-04 when management blamed client-led conversion delays at fewer than 10 large banks and announced CFO James Kehoe's exit. Screen quirk: the metrics row uses stale FY2023 data (with Worldpay); on 2026 guidance FCF is $2.15-2.25B, about 16% of market cap and 6.5% of EV, so the name still qualifies on real numbers.
key_numbers: Adj P/E ~4.6 (on $5.85 2026 guide); FCF 2026 guide $2.15-2.25B = ~16% of mcap, ~6.5% of EV; debt $20.8B vs mcap $13.8B; pro forma growth 3.1-3.6%; adj EBITDA margin 42.9%; -68.9% from 3y high

name: EPAM Systems, Inc.
one_line_reason: A former 20%-a-year engineering-hours business now grows 2.5% organically and its time-and-materials revenue is shrinking, which is exactly what AI coding tools do to billable hours; the buybacks mask a business whose unit of sale is getting smaller.
evidence: Q3 2026 revenue rose 2.3% to $1.426B (2.5% organic constant currency) and full-year 2026 organic growth is guided at 2.5-2.7% (EX-99.1, 8-K filed 2026-11-05); ten-year revenue CAGR was 19.6%. Time-and-materials revenue fell to $1,106M from $1,119M a year earlier and Americas T&M fell 3.9% to $637M, while fixed-price rose 18% to $316M (10-Q filed 2026-11-05); nine-month operating cash flow dropped to $250M from $372M. Management is leaning on capital return: a $500M ASR partly on the revolver, a new $1.8B authorization and a pledge to return at least 50% of FCF in 2027-2029.
key_numbers: P/E 20.8 GAAP vs 44.2 10y median (~18x 2026 GAAP EPS guide $8.41-8.49); fwd non-GAAP P/E 10.8; FCF-SBC yield 5.5%; organic growth 2.5% vs 19.6% 10y CAGR; T&M revenue -1.2% y/y; ROIC 14.6% vs 31.1% 5y avg; short interest 18%

name: Accenture plc
one_line_reason: The market de-rated Accenture from 24x to 16x on the fear that AI hollows out paid consulting hours, but FY26 revenue growth accelerated to 7% in local currency in Q4 and outsourcing bookings run well ahead of revenue, so the damage so far is to the multiple, not the business.
evidence: FY26 (to 2026-08-31) revenue rose 5% in local currency to $74.18B, above the 3-4% guide, and Q4 rose 7% LC to $18.68B; FY26 bookings were $84.5B (book-to-bill 1.1) with Q4 managed-services book-to-bill of 1.4; FY27 guide is 3-6% LC growth and GAAP EPS $14.39-14.81 (EX-99, 8-K filed 2026-10-01). Headcount rose to about 814,000 with nearly 110,000 AI and data practitioners, and the 10-K risk factors now say AI 'could harm the company's business, including by reducing demand for our services' and that clients may not accept new pricing models (10-K filed 2026). Cash returned rose 38% to $11.5B in FY26, including $7.5B of buybacks.
key_numbers: P/E 16.1 vs 24.4 10y median; EV/EBIT 11.5 vs 17.4; FCF-SBC yield 7.1%; FY26 LC growth 5% (Q4 7%); FY27 guide 3-6%; ROIC 29.7%; net cash $2.7B; -40.6% from 3y high
